bounded_statement: The report's selected conclusion (rejection of chance performance at the 0.05 level, p = 0.0414) rests on an exact binomial test that pools all 20 trial rows as independent observations, even though the data description designates fish_tag as the independent unit and each of the 5 fish contributes 4 rows. Each independent unit therefore enters the row-independent binomial procedure four times. This is material within the supplied files: per-fish hit rates are 1.00, 1.00, 0.75, 0.75, 0.25, and unit-respecting analyses at n = 5 fish (e.g., one-sample t-test on per-fish rates vs 0.5, p ≈ 0.14; sign test, p ≈ 0.375) do not reject chance, so the reported significance depends on the improper pooling.

counterevidence_considered.description: The workflow and report are transparent about the pooling: they compute and display a per-fish tally and explicitly state that no grouping was applied, so the repeated-unit entry is disclosed rather than hidden. This transparency does not, however, make the pooled test's independence assumption valid or the significance claim supported.

evidence.description: The per-fish tally in the report shows strong between-fish heterogeneity (two fish at 4/4, one fish at 1/4), demonstrating that trials cluster by fish and are not exchangeable across the pooled sequence; a fish-level analysis of these five rates (1.00, 1.00, 0.75, 0.75, 0.25) does not reject chance (t-test p ~ 0.14, sign test p ~ 0.375), so the pooled p = 0.0414 is not robust to respecting the independent unit.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the finding in three ways. (1) Checked whether each independent unit actually enters the test more than once: the CSV and the description both confirm 4 rows per fish for all 5 fish, so repeated entry is established. (2) Checked whether the pooling could be harmless because within-fish trials behave as exchangeable coin flips: the per-fish tallies (4/4, 4/4, 3/4, 3/4, 1/4) show marked clustering by fish, so the independence assumption of the pooled binomial test is contradicted by the data itself. (3) Checked whether the report's conclusion would survive a unit-respecting reanalysis: on the 5 per-fish hit rates (1.00, 1.00, 0.75, 0.75, 0.25), a one-sample t-test against 0.5 gives t ~ 1.83, df = 4, p ~ 0.14, and an exact sign test (4 of 5 fish above 0.5) gives two-sided p = 0.375; neither rejects chance at 0.05, so the reported rejection depends entirely on the improper pooling. All three falsification routes failed, supporting the demonstrated-issue verdict.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py computes the test statistic as binomtest(count_hits(rows), len(rows), CHANCE_RATE) over all 20 rows, treating each row as an independent Bernoulli observation. Because each of the 5 fish (the declared independent unit) contributes 4 rows, within-fish correlation is ignored; the effective sample of independent units is 5, not 20, inflating the effective n and producing a p-value (0.0414) that crosses the 0.05 threshold when fish-level analyses would not. The per-fish tally in the report (4/4, 4/4, 3/4, 3/4, 1/4) shows marked between-fish heterogeneity, confirming rows within a fish are not exchangeable.
